Hi team —

Quick note ahead of today's 3pm sync: Orion (DEAL-3487) has pushed a potential pilot start into August. They are asking for a short ramp of reserved slots (3 x p4d-equivalent) during their pilot month and then a larger reserved commitment if pilot KPIs look good. We need to align on the tradeoffs between:

- short-term burst + prefix caching vs. reserving slots immediately
- expected incremental burn on hosted model weights (we have two viable variants)
- SLA risk if we re-route to lower-cost variants during peak

I've attached the latest run-rate workbook (fleet_run_rate_v2.xlsx) and Orion's capacity doc. Agenda attached in meeting-agenda.md. Please skim the numbers and flag any blockers before 2:30pm so I can circulate a single slide for Finance + Sales.

Ask: can Finance (Laura) confirm acceptable temporary burn thresholds for pilots (percentage of monthly committed GPU spend we can tolerate) and can Infra (Jordan/Dylan) confirm fallback latency/throughput hit if we move to the q8 quantized variant?

Thanks — will summarize in a follow-up for the executive note.

— Mina

Mina — thanks, looked through the workbook. A few quick flags:

- The pilot profile from Orion shows 40% of peak tokens during weekday business hours and a long tail overnight. If we rely on burst only, the projected P95 latency for the hosted variant climbs ~35% during peak.
- If we commit 3 reserved slots as they requested, our incremental monthly burn (based on current pricing) is ~$36k/mo, front-loaded.
- Alternative: start pilot on a cached prefix with 2 reserved + 1 burst slot — saves ~18% of burn while keeping P95 within our SLO window for demos.

I put my annotated rows in the run_rate sheet (column 'ben_notes'). Jordan/Dylan — can you validate the expected P95 delta for q8 variant if we need to fall back?

Also, should Sales try to get pilot acceptance criteria tightened to a 3-week measurable window? Shorter pilots reduce risk.

-Ben

Sarah — thanks. Quick answers and proposals:

- P95 deltas: Infra team (Jordan/Dylan) measured an approximate +30–40% P95 hit on the hosted high-quality variant during sustained peaks. The q8 variant shows a +15–20% hit but with ~22% lower cost per token. Jordan, attaching the microbench report from the staging runs (see orion_capacity_requirements.pdf).
- Instrumentation: we can surface token-level cost in the pilot via a short telemetry hook — Laura, we need a signoff on data retention for the telemetry (7 days) and whether Finance can accept a rolling pilot burn reconciliation.
- Recommended approach: 2 reserved slots + 1 burst slot for pilot start, enable KV caching for the 2 heaviest prefixes, and add a hard fallback to q8 if availability drops below 80% for two consecutive hours. This keeps demo latencies tolerable and limits committed spend.

Action items (I will own):
- Circulate single-slide summary for Execs by 2:30pm (will include the numbers Ben annotated).
- Draft an addendum for procurement outlining the 3-week acceptance criteria + fallback language (to share with Sarah/Kyle).

Attachments: updated run-rate and the microbench pdf.

Mina / team —

Finance POV: temporary pilot burn increases are acceptable under two constraints:

1) Total additional spend for the pilot must not exceed 20% of the customer's expected first-quarter committed spend (we'll accept a one-time variance for demo purposes). For DEAL-3487 that's a hard cap of $40k for the pilot month.
2) We need automated cost alerts and a weekly reconciliation sheet (HubSpot + the run-rate sheet).

If we put the pilot on 2 reserved + 1 burst, I estimate projected incremental spend of ~$32k/mo which fits the cap with some buffer. Approve the KV caching approach — that will lower run-rate risk.

Laura Bennett
